theory.intro: A solution of $f(x)=g(x)$ is an $x$-value where the two graphs cross. Sketching each side shows how many solutions a domain holds, even for equations no algebraic method can solve.
facts: A horizontal line $y=m$ misses the curve completely when $m$ lies outside the range of the wave.
A line that just touches the curve at a maximum or a minimum gives one solution there, not two.
Because the wave repeats, adding the period to any solution gives another solution.
Two solutions either side of a maximum at $x=M$ are symmetric about it, so a solution $x=p$ is paired with $x=2M-p$.
A line $y=mx+c$ can only meet $y=k\sin x + d$ where the height of the line lies between the minimum and the maximum of the wave.
steps: Sketch each side of the equation on the same axes
Count the points of intersection inside the domain
Read or calculate the $x$-coordinate of one intersection
Use symmetry and the period to reach the remaining solutions

foundation.question_text:
The graph of $y = 2\sin x$ and the line $y = 1$ are shown for $0 \le x \le 4\pi$.
[tikz]
\begin{tikzpicture}[every node/.style={font=\large}]
\begin{axis}[axis lines=middle, xlabel={$x$}, ylabel={$y$},
  xmin=-0.6, xmax=13.6, ymin=-2.6, ymax=2.6,
  xtick={3.1416, 6.2832, 9.4248, 12.5664},
  xticklabels={$\pi$, $2\pi$, $3\pi$, $4\pi$},
  ytick={-2, 1, 2},
  samples=200, clip=false,
  axis line style={-{Stealth}}, width=11cm, height=6.5cm]
\addplot[smooth, thick, blue, domain=0:12.5664] {2*sin(deg(x))};
\addplot[thick, red, domain=0:12.5664] {1};
\end{axis}
\end{tikzpicture}
[/tikz]
How many solutions does $2\sin x = 1$ have for $0 \le x \le 4\pi$? List them.
foundation.solution_text:
The domain $0 \le x \le 4\pi$ contains two complete cycles, and the line cuts each cycle twice.
There are $4$ points of intersection, so there are $4$ solutions.
$\sin x = \dfrac{1}{2}$
In the first cycle: $x = \dfrac{\pi}{6},\ \dfrac{5\pi}{6}$
Adding the period $2\pi$ to each gives the second cycle.
$x = \dfrac{\pi}{6},\ \dfrac{5\pi}{6},\ \dfrac{13\pi}{6},\ \dfrac{17\pi}{6}$

foundation.question_text:
The graph of $y = 3\cos(2x)$ and the line $y = -3$ are shown for $0 \le x \le 2\pi$.

\begin{tikzpicture}[every node/.style={font=\large}]

  xmin=-0.3, xmax=6.9, ymin=-4, ymax=4,
  xtick={1.5708, 3.1416, 4.7124, 6.2832},
  xticklabels={$\frac{\pi}{2}$, $\pi$, $\frac{3\pi}{2}$, $2\pi$},
  ytick={-3, 3},
  samples=200, clip=false,
  axis line style={-{Stealth}}, width=11cm, height=6.5cm]
\addplot[smooth, thick, blue, domain=0:6.2832] {3*cos(deg(2*x))};
\addplot[thick, red, domain=0:6.2832] {-3};
\end{axis}
\end{tikzpicture}
[/tikz]
How many solutions does $3\cos(2x) = -3$ have for $0 \le x \le 2\pi$, and why is the answer not four?
foundation.solution_text:
The line sits at the minimum value of the curve, so it touches the curve rather than crossing it.
Each cycle therefore contributes one point of intersection, not two.
The domain holds two cycles, so there are $2$ points of intersection.
$\cos(2x) = -1$
$2x = \pi,\ 3\pi$
$x = \dfrac{\pi}{2},\ \dfrac{3\pi}{2}$

foundation.question_text:
The graph of $y = \sin(3x)$ and the line $y = \dfrac{1}{2}$ are shown for $0 \le x \le 2\pi$.
[tikz]
\begin{tikzpicture}[every node/.style={font=\large}]
\begin{axis}[axis lines=middle, xlabel={$x$}, ylabel={$y$},
  xmin=-0.3, xmax=6.9, ymin=-1.6, ymax=1.6,
  xtick={1.5708, 3.1416, 4.7124, 6.2832},
  xticklabels={$\frac{\pi}{2}$, $\pi$, $\frac{3\pi}{2}$, $2\pi$},
  ytick={-1, 1},
  samples=200, clip=false,
  axis line style={-{Stealth}}, width=11cm, height=6.5cm]
\addplot[smooth, thick, blue, domain=0:6.2832] {sin(deg(3*x))};
\addplot[thick, red, domain=0:6.2832] {0.5};
\node[red, anchor=west] at (axis cs:6.45,0.5) {$y=\frac{1}{2}$};
\end{axis}
\end{tikzpicture}
[/tikz]
How many solutions does $\sin(3x) = \dfrac{1}{2}$ have for $0 \le x \le 2\pi$? Explain how the period gives the count.
foundation.solution_text:
Period $=\dfrac{2\pi}{3}$
The domain $0 \le x \le 2\pi$ is three complete cycles.
$\dfrac{2\pi}{\frac{2\pi}{3}} = 3$
The line $y=\dfrac{1}{2}$ lies between $-1$ and $1$, so it cuts each cycle twice.
There are $6$ points of intersection, so the equation has $6$ solutions.

One solution of $4\sin x = 3$ is $x \approx 0.848$. Use the symmetry of the curve to find the other solution in $0 \le x \le 2\pi$, correct to three decimal places.
foundation.solution_text:
The maximum of $y = 4\sin x$ in this domain is at $x = \dfrac{\pi}{2}$.
The two intersections are symmetric about that maximum.
$x = 2\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right) - 0.848$
$= \pi - 0.848$
$= 2.294$

foundation.question_text:
The graph of $y = 2\cos\left(\dfrac{\pi x}{6}\right)$ and the line $y = 1$ are shown for $0 \le x \le 24$.
[tikz]
\begin{tikzpicture}[every node/.style={font=\large}]
\begin{axis}[axis lines=middle, xlabel={$x$}, ylabel={$y$},
  xmin=-1, xmax=26, ymin=-2.6, ymax=2.6,
  xtick={6, 12, 18, 24},
  ytick={-2, 1, 2},
  samples=200, clip=false,
  axis line style={-{Stealth}}, width=12cm, height=6.5cm]
\addplot[smooth, thick, blue, domain=0:24] {2*cos(deg(pi*x/6))};
\addplot[thick, red, domain=0:24] {1};
\end{axis}
\end{tikzpicture}
[/tikz]
The curve has period $12$, and $x=2$ is one solution of $2\cos\left(\dfrac{\pi x}{6}\right)=1$. Find all solutions in $0 \le x \le 24$.
foundation.solution_text:
The minimum of the first cycle is at $x=6$, and the pair of intersections either side of it is symmetric about it.
$x = 2(6) - 2$
$= 10$
Adding the period $12$ to each of $x=2$ and $x=10$ gives the second cycle.
$2+12 = 14$
$10+12 = 22$
$x = 2,\ 10,\ 14,\ 22$

How many solutions does $\sin(2x) = \dfrac{x}{2}-\dfrac{1}{4}$ have in $-\pi \le x \le \pi$, and how many of them are positive?
foundation.solution_text:
Each crossing of the curve and the line is one solution.
The graphs cross three times inside $-\pi \le x \le \pi$, so there are $3$ solutions.
Two of the crossings lie to the left of the $y$-axis and one lies to the right.
Only $1$ solution is positive.

foundation.question_text:
The curve $y = 3\sin x$ and the line $y = 2-x$ are shown for $-2\pi \le x \le 2\pi$.
[tikz]
\begin{tikzpicture}[every node/.style={font=\large}]
\begin{axis}[axis lines=middle, xlabel={$x$}, ylabel={$y$},
  xmin=-7, xmax=7, ymin=-4.8, ymax=4.8,
  xtick={-6.2832, -3.1416, 3.1416, 6.2832},
  xticklabels={$-2\pi$, $-\pi$, $\pi$, $2\pi$},
  ytick={-3, 3},
  samples=200, clip=false,
  axis line style={-{Stealth}}, width=12cm, height=6.5cm]
\addplot[smooth, thick, blue, domain=-6.2832:6.2832] {3*sin(deg(x))};
\addplot[thick, red, domain=-2.6:6.6] {2-x};
\end{axis}
\end{tikzpicture}
[/tikz]
Show that every solution of $3\sin x = 2-x$ must satisfy $-1 \le x \le 5$.
foundation.solution_text:
Since $-1 \le \sin x \le 1$:
$-3 \le 3\sin x \le 3$
At a solution, $2-x$ equals $3\sin x$, so it must lie in the same interval.
$-3 \le 2-x \le 3$
$-5 \le -x \le 1$
$-1 \le x \le 5$
Outside this interval the line lies above or below every point of the curve, so no solution is possible.

How many solutions does $2\cos x = 1-\dfrac{x}{2}$ have, and explain why no solution can lie outside $-2 \le x \le 6$.
development.solution_text:
The graphs cross three times, so the equation has $3$ solutions.
Since $-1 \le \cos x \le 1$:
$-2 \le 2\cos x \le 2$
$-2 \le 1-\dfrac{x}{2} \le 2$
$-3 \le -\dfrac{x}{2} \le 1$
$-2 \le x \le 6$
Beyond these values the line is higher than the curve's maximum or lower than its minimum, so the graphs cannot meet.

The function has period $12$ and a minimum at $x=6$. Given that $x = 1.77$ is a solution of $f(x)=6$, find the other solutions in $0 \le x \le 24$, correct to two decimal places.
development.solution_text:
The first two intersections are symmetric about the minimum at $x=6$.
$x = 2(6) - 1.77$
$= 10.23$
Adding the period $12$ to each of these gives the second cycle.
$1.77 + 12 = 13.77$
$10.23 + 12 = 22.23$
The other solutions are $x = 10.23,\ 13.77,\ 22.23$.

\addplot[thick, red, domain=3.1416:8] {(x-3.1416)/4};

\end{tikzpicture}
[/tikz]
How many solutions does $\cos x = \left|\dfrac{x-\pi}{4}\right|$ have over all real values of $x$? Justify your answer from the graphs.
development.solution_text:
The two arms of $y = \left|\dfrac{x-\pi}{4}\right|$ rise from $0$ at $x=\pi$, and reach $1$ when $x = \pi-4$ and $x = \pi+4$.
Beyond those two values the V-shape is above $1$, which is higher than any point of $y=\cos x$.
So every solution lies in $\pi-4 \le x \le \pi+4$, and this is the region drawn.
The graphs cross four times inside it, twice on each arm.
There are $4$ solutions.

The curve has period $\dfrac{\pi}{\frac{1}{2}} = 2\pi$, so the domain holds two cycles and the line cuts each once.
There are $2$ points of intersection.
$\tan\left(\dfrac{x}{2}\right) = 1$
Let $u = \dfrac{x}{2}$, so $0 \le u \le 2\pi$.
$u = \dfrac{\pi}{4},\ \dfrac{5\pi}{4}$
$x = 2u$
$x = \dfrac{\pi}{2},\ \dfrac{5\pi}{2}$

mastery.question_text:
The curve $y = 1+\sin\left(\dfrac{\pi x}{2}\right)$ is shown for $0 \le x \le 4$.
[tikz]
\begin{tikzpicture}[every node/.style={font=\large}]
\begin{axis}[axis lines=middle, xlabel={$x$}, ylabel={$y$},
  xmin=-0.4, xmax=4.8, ymin=-0.5, ymax=2.6,
  xtick={1, 2, 3, 4},
  ytick={1, 2},
  samples=200, clip=false,
  axis line style={-{Stealth}}, width=10cm, height=6.5cm]
\addplot[smooth, thick, blue, domain=0:4] {1+sin(deg(pi*x/2))};
\end{axis}
\end{tikzpicture}
[/tikz]
The equation $\sin\left(\dfrac{\pi x}{2}\right) = mx-1$ can be rewritten as $1+\sin\left(\dfrac{\pi x}{2}\right) = mx$, so its solutions are where the line $y=mx$ meets the curve above. Find the values of $m$ for which the equation has exactly one solution in $0 \le x \le 4$.
mastery.solution_text:
Every line $y=mx$ passes through the origin, which is below the curve since the curve starts at $(0,1)$.
If $m<0$ the line is negative for $x>0$, while the curve is never negative, so there is no intersection.
If $m=0$ the line is the $x$-axis, which touches the curve only at its minimum $(3,0)$, giving exactly one solution.
For $m>0$ the line always crosses the curve once between $x=0$ and $x=3$, because the curve drops from $1$ to $0$ while the line rises.
A second crossing after $x=3$ happens only while the line is still below the curve at $x=4$.
The line through $(0,0)$ and $(4,1)$ has gradient $\dfrac{1}{4}$.
$m = 0.25$
For $0 < m \le 0.25$ the line meets the curve twice, and for $m > 0.25$ it meets it only once.
$m = 0$ or $m > 0.25$

mastery.question_text:
The graph of $f(x) = 8\cos\left(\dfrac{\pi x}{9}\right)+5$ and the line $y = 10$ are shown for $0 \le x \le 36$.
[tikz]
\begin{tikzpicture}[every node/.style={font=\large}]
\begin{axis}[axis lines=middle, xlabel={$x$}, ylabel={$y$},
  xmin=-1.5, xmax=39, ymin=-4.5, ymax=14.5,
  xtick={9, 18, 27, 36},
  ytick={-3, 5, 10, 13},
  samples=200, clip=false,
  axis line style={-{Stealth}}, width=12cm, height=6.5cm]
\addplot[smooth, thick, blue, domain=0:36] {8*cos(deg(pi*x/9))+5};
\addplot[thick, red, domain=0:36] {10};
\end{axis}
\end{tikzpicture}
[/tikz]
The function has period $18$, with maxima at $x=0$, $x=18$ and $x=36$. Given that $x \approx 2.57$ is a solution of $f(x)=10$, find all the solutions in $0 \le x \le 36$, correct to two decimal places.
mastery.solution_text:
The first minimum is at $x=9$, and the first pair of intersections is symmetric about it.
$x = 2(9) - 2.57$
$= 15.43$
Adding the period $18$ to each of these gives the second cycle.
$2.57 + 18 = 20.57$
$15.43 + 18 = 33.43$
All four values lie inside $0 \le x \le 36$.
$x = 2.57,\ 15.43,\ 20.57,\ 33.43$

mastery.question_text:
The curve $y = 4\cos(2x)$ and the line $y = x-1$ are shown for $-3 \le x \le 5$.
[tikz]
\begin{tikzpicture}[every node/.style={font=\large}]
\begin{axis}[axis lines=middle, xlabel={$x$}, ylabel={$y$},
  xmin=-4, xmax=6, ymin=-5.5, ymax=5.5,
  xtick={-3, -1, 1, 3, 5},
  ytick={-4, 4},
  samples=200, clip=false,
  axis line style={-{Stealth}}, width=12cm, height=6.5cm]
\addplot[smooth, thick, blue, domain=-3:5] {4*cos(deg(2*x))};
\addplot[thick, red, domain=-3:5] {x-1};
\end{axis}
\end{tikzpicture}
[/tikz]
Show that every solution of $4\cos(2x) = x-1$ satisfies $-3 \le x \le 5$, and hence state how many solutions the equation has.
mastery.solution_text:
Since $-1 \le \cos(2x) \le 1$:
$-4 \le 4\cos(2x) \le 4$
At a solution, $x-1$ takes the same value as $4\cos(2x)$.
$-4 \le x-1 \le 4$
$-3 \le x \le 5$
So the whole picture is drawn: outside this interval the line is beyond the reach of the curve.
The curve has period $\pi$, so the interval of length $8$ holds about two and a half cycles, and the graphs cross five times.
There are $5$ solutions.
